reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) confirms oxygen incorporation forms a core–shell structure and reports coercivity values of 23 A/m for CoCrFeNiO0.4 and 223 A/m for CoCrFeNiO0.8, but it does not explicitly state that the oxide shell increases magnetic anisotropy energy or that the coercivity increase is due to hindered domain wall motion—these mechanistic claims are inferred rather than directly supported.
premises: Oxygen incorporation in CoCrFeNi films forms a core–shell structure with ferromagnetic cores and Cr-oxide shells
The oxide shell increases magnetic anisotropy energy, raising the coercive field
CoCrFeNiO0.8 film shows higher coercivity (223 A/m) than low-oxygen films (23 A/m)
The coercivity increase is due to the oxide shell hindering domain wall motion
